perspective:
Christian has access to the following information:

- He is a police officer. Jonathan is his childhood best friend, someone he trusts and often seeks advice from; Jonathan is more educated and Christian values his perspective.
- Christian feels Jonathan has been hiding something important. This makes him anxious and suspicious.
- Christian arranges and attends a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop to confront him.
- Christian hears Jonathan admit that Jonathan is in some trouble and had not known how to tell him.
- Christian feels worried and empathetic, offers help and support, and tells Jonathan they can face it together.
- Christian hears Jonathan say:
  - The situation is complicated.
  - He does not want to drag Christian into it.
  - He could use support and resources.
  - He needs to find a way out of the mess.
- Christian begins to suspect Jonathan’s trouble may be related to criminal activity. He feels conflicted and concerned.
- Christian asks Jonathan if the trouble is illegal. He hears Jonathan say:
  - He cannot say for sure.
  - He might have gotten involved with the wrong people.
  - He did not do anything illegal himself.
- Christian tells Jonathan he will look into the matter discreetly. He hears Jonathan thank him and say he trusts Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his own investigation, Christian learns/believes Jonathan is being framed. He feels determined and protective.
- Christian tells Jonathan he believes someone is trying to set Jonathan up. He hears Jonathan ask who would do that.
- Christian says he is not sure yet but has leads, and he plans to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Christian hears Jonathan thank him and say he does not know what he would do without him.
- Christian comes to believe/find out that the real culprit is someone close to both him and Jonathan, someone they both know and trust. He feels betrayed and resolute.
- Christian tells Jonathan he found out who is behind it and that it is someone they both know and trust.
- Christian plans to confront the real culprit and bring them to justice. He hears Jonathan warn him that the person is dangerous but say he trusts Christian to do what is right.
- The provided dialogue does not name the real culprit.
